cards.name: Blend
cards.summary: Interactive Blend tool: drag from one object to another and CorelDRAW builds a live group of intermediate steps that morph shape, outline and colour from the start object to the end object. Editing either end object updates the whole blend.
cards.how: Pick the tool, press on the start object and drag onto the end object; release to create the blend. Hold Alt while dragging to draw a freehand path the blend follows. On the property bar set the number of steps (or a fixed spacing when the blend runs along a path), blend direction (rotation), loop blend, colour blend direction (direct / clockwise / counter-clockwise around the colour wheel), object and colour acceleration, and Path properties (New Path, then click a curve, to run the blend along it). Drag the start or end object to re-shape the run; with the blend selected, use Object > Break Apart when the steps must be edited one by one.
cards.script_api: The drag cannot be scripted, the result can. Activate the tool: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "d72c98e8-59be-4a31-b9db-1d0e83bdd218" or Application.ActiveTool = 74 (cdrToolBlend). Build the blend in the object model instead: StartShape.CreateBlend(Shape, Steps=20, ColorBlendType, Mode, Spacing, Angle, Loop, Path, RotateShapes, SpacingAccel, ColorAccel, AccelSize) on IVGShape, returns an IVGEffect.
use_for: smooth vector shading between two shapes (highlights on a logo, glossy buttons)
rainbow / stripe line art and guilloche patterns
stacked 3D-look headline type made from many offset copies
evenly spaced dots or icons along a curve (blend on a path)
colour step charts and swatch ramps
avoid: a plain linear or radial colour transition on one shape: use a fountain fill (Interactive Fill), it prints lighter
identical copies with no morph: use Step and Repeat
start and end objects with very different node structures twist mid-blend: match node counts or map start/end nodes first
hundreds of steps on complex objects bloat the file and slow output and RIPs; keep steps just high enough to look smooth

review.changes: how: 'Object > Break Blend Apart' is not a harvested command; replaced with the harvested Object > Break Apart (with the blend selected)

cards.name: Block Shadow
cards.summary: Block Shadow tool: drag from an object to add a solid, flat vector shadow block that extends from it in one direction (a hard long shadow in one colour, no blur or shading). Exact property-bar option names were not harvested, so treat the option list below as unverified.
cards.how: Pick the tool and drag from the object in the direction and length the shadow should run; the shadow stays linked to the object and updates when it changes. On the property bar adjust depth, direction (angle) and the block colour; options such as an outline on the block, simplify and remove holes are expected there but were not read from this install. Convert or break the shadow apart when it must become an ordinary editable curve.
cards.script_api: Only selecting the tool can be scripted: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "249b7791-6d54-401b-a326-378c53773a52". Application.ActiveTool read back -1 for this tool (no cdrTools value), and no object-model call that creates a block shadow was found in the harvested API, so the shadow itself has to be dragged by hand.
use_for: flat long-shadow headline and icon styles
retro / sign-painter block lettering
vinyl-cut, screen-print and embroidery artwork that needs one solid vector shape instead of a soft bitmap shadow
avoid: soft, feathered or transparent shadows: use the Shadow tool
depth with shaded sides and perspective: use the Extrude tool
automated builds: there is no scripted way to create it, so draw the block as a curve (or use Extrude) when a script must make it

cards.name: Contour
cards.summary: Contour tool: adds a live series of evenly spaced concentric copies of an object's outline, stepping outward, inward, or all the way to the centre, with fill and outline colours graded from the original to the last step.
cards.how: Pick the tool and drag from the object's edge outward (outside contour) or toward its centre (inside contour). On the property bar choose To Center / Inside / Outside, set the number of steps and the offset between them, the colour direction (linear, clockwise, counter-clockwise), the outline and fill colour of the last step, object and colour acceleration, and the corner type (mitred, round, bevelled). With the contour selected, Object > Break Apart turns the steps into separate editable objects (for example a single outside step as a cut line).
cards.script_api: The drag cannot be scripted, the result can. Activate the tool: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "441d6b88-877e-4d00-951f-4521b9987650" or Application.ActiveTool = 113 (cdrToolContour). Create the effect directly: Shape.CreateContour(Direction=1, Offset, Steps=1, BlendType, OutlineColor, FillColor, FillColor2, SpacingAccel, ColorAccel, EndCapType, CornerType, MiterLimit) on IVGShape, returns an IVGEffect.
use_for: sticker and die-cut outlines (one outside step, then break apart)
neon / multi-stroke outline text
topographic and ripple line patterns
bleed or keyline offsets around a logo
avoid: a single offset outline that must stay as plain geometry: break the contour apart afterwards or the outline stays tied to the source
very small offsets on detailed text produce clogged, self-overlapping steps; simplify the shape or use fewer steps
morphing between two different shapes: use the Blend tool

review.changes: how: 'Object > Break Contour Apart' is not a harvested command; replaced with the harvested Object > Break Apart

cards.name: Distort
cards.summary: Distort tool: applies a live distortion to a vector object or text in one of three modes chosen on the property bar: Push and Pull (edges pushed in to spiky pucker or pulled out to rounded petals), Zipper (saw-tooth / zig-zag edges) and Twister (swirl around a centre).
cards.how: Pick the tool, choose the mode on the property bar, then drag on the object: the press point sets the distortion origin and the drag length sets the amount. Push and Pull: drag one way to push, the other to pull, amplitude on the property bar. Zipper: amplitude and frequency, plus Random, Smooth and Local options. Twister: direction plus complete rotations and extra degrees. Center Distortion puts the origin in the middle; Add New Distortion stacks another one; Clear Distortion removes it; convert to curves to make it permanent.
cards.script_api: The drag cannot be scripted, the result can. Activate the tool: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "f42edc69-976b-4917-802a-1c4fed6297ef" or Application.ActiveTool = 79 (cdrToolDistortion). Create the effect directly on IVGShape: Shape.CreatePushPullDistortion(OriginX, OriginY, Amplitude), Shape.CreateZipperDistortion(OriginX, OriginY, Amplitude, Frequency, Random, Smooth, Local) or Shape.CreateTwisterDistortion(OriginX, OriginY, Angle); each returns an IVGEffect.
use_for: starburst sale badges and comic burst shapes from a circle (Zipper or Push and Pull)
flower and petal shapes (Pull)
swirls and twisted ornaments (Twister)
rough, torn or jagged edges on shapes and display text (Zipper with Random)
avoid: a precise regular star or polygon: use the Star or Polygon tool
warping a whole shape or headline into an arch or bulge: use the Envelope tool
large amplitudes on complex text make unreadable spikes; keep it for short words or simple shapes

cards.name: Envelope
cards.summary: Envelope tool: wraps an object or text in an editable dashed bounding shape with nodes; dragging the envelope's nodes and segments bends the contents to fit, giving arches, bulges, waves, flags and custom silhouettes while the text stays editable.
cards.how: Pick the tool and click the object; drag the envelope nodes or segments to reshape it. On the property bar pick the mode (Straight Line, Single Arc, Double Arc, Unconstrained), the mapping mode (Horizontal, Original, Putty, Vertical), Keep Lines to stop straight lines bending, and envelope presets. Create Envelope From copies the shape of another object you click. Clear Envelope removes it; convert to curves to make it permanent.
cards.script_api: The node dragging cannot be scripted, the result can. Activate the tool with FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "1f16cb33-9819-4fa7-a3cd-5c4d61ba2db2" (preferred). Application.ActiveTool = 29 also enters the Envelope state, but 29 is outside the cdrTools enum and the toolbox then highlighted Freehand Pick (fb9a380a-4bbb-23bd-4e45-2eeed3e485b1), so do not rely on the toolbox read-back. Create the effect on IVGShape: Shape.CreateEnvelope(PresetIndex, Mode=2, KeepLines), Shape.CreateEnvelopeFromShape(Source, Mode, KeepLines, CopyMode, CornerIndices) or Shape.CreateEnvelopeFromCurve(Source, ...), each returns an IVGEffect.
use_for: arched and bulged headline text on posters and badges
fitting a word or logo into a shield, banner or bottle-label silhouette (Create Envelope From)
flag and wave warps on vector artwork
squeezing type into an irregular frame while it stays editable
avoid: true one- or two-point perspective: use Object > Perspective > Add Perspective
text that should run along a curve with upright, undistorted letters: use Fit Text to Path
small text under strong envelopes becomes distorted and hard to read; keep it for display sizes

review.changes: avoid: 'Effects > Add Perspective' is the wrong menu path; the harvested path is Object > Perspective > Add Perspective

cards.name: Extrude
cards.summary: Extrude tool: gives a flat vector object or text vector 3D depth by projecting its sides toward a vanishing point, producing shaded side faces that stay live (editable depth, rotation, colour, bevel and lighting).
cards.how: Pick the tool and drag from the object in the direction the depth should go; the X marker is the vanishing point, drag it to change the direction and the slider to change the depth. On the property bar choose the extrusion type (small/big back, small/big front, back/front parallel), depth, vanishing point properties (locked to object or page, copied or shared between objects), 3D rotation, extrusion colour (use object fill, solid or shaded), bevels and lighting (light sources and intensity).
cards.script_api: The drag cannot be scripted, the result can. Activate the tool: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "c5555cfc-1c54-4c5b-ad28-60a4ec569798" or Application.ActiveTool = 73 (cdrToolInteractiveExtrude; set and read back confirmed by the 2026-10-04 audit). Create the effect on IVGShape: Shape.CreateExtrude(Type, VPType, VPX, VPY, Depth=20, Shading, BaseColor, ShadingColor, BevelDepth, BevelAngle=45, BevelColor, BevelOnly), returns an IVGEffect.
use_for: retro 3D block lettering for posters and titles
signage and logo marks with visible depth
simple vector 3D solids (boxes, bars, isometric-looking icons) that stay editable and print sharp
avoid: photoreal or textured 3D: build it in a 3D app or Photoshop
a flat single-colour long shadow: use Block Shadow, which makes one simple shape
lighting and bevels on complex text create many objects and slow the file; break apart and simplify before sending to print or cutters

cards.name: Shadow
cards.summary: Shadow tool (cdrToolDropShadow): drags a soft, feathered, semi-transparent shadow off an object, either flat behind it or as a perspective cast shadow on the ground; the shadow is a live effect linked to the object and is rendered as a bitmap.
cards.how: Pick the tool and drag from the object's centre to offset a flat drop shadow, or from an edge (top / bottom / side) to cast a perspective shadow. On the property bar set presets, shadow colour, opacity, feathering width and direction, feather edge type, the merge (transparency) mode, offset, and for perspective shadows the angle, stretch and fade. The property bar also switches the tool between Drop Shadow and Inner Shadow (the harvest lists both as modes of this tool). With the shadowed object selected, Object > Break Apart turns the shadow into a separate bitmap.
cards.script_api: The drag cannot be scripted, the result can. Activate the tool: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "e65d1597-722d-4afb-82fe-964d7ddff531" or Application.ActiveTool = 80 (cdrToolDropShadow). Create the shadow on IVGShape: Shape.CreateDropShadow(Type, Opacity=50, Feather=15, OffsetX, OffsetY, Color, FeatherType, FeatherEdge, PerspectiveAngle=-45, PerspectiveStretch=1, Fade, MergeMode); inner shadows use Shape.CreateInnerShadow(Opacity, Feather, OffsetX, OffsetY, Color, FeatherType, FeatherEdge, MergeMode, Depth). Both return an IVGEffect.
use_for: lifting text and cut-out products off a busy background
perspective ground shadows under product shots and packaging mockups
soft card and button shadows in web and social graphics
avoid: vinyl cutting, embroidery or spot-colour screen printing: the shadow is a transparent bitmap; use Block Shadow for a solid vector shadow
very large feathered shadows at high resolution bloat the PDF and slow the RIP; flatten or lower the shadow resolution
hard flat long shadows: use Block Shadow

review.changes: how: removed the invented 'CorelDRAW 2022 and later' version claim (harvest lists Drop Shadow and Inner Shadow as modes of this tool in 25.1); 'Object > Break Shadow Group Apart' replaced with the harvested Object > Break Apart
